en: The Philippine eagle, the national bird, possesses a shaggy crest and hunts monkeys in the canopy of Mindanao's dipterocarp forests.
The sampaguita, our national flower, releases its sweet fragrance primarily at night to attract pollinating hawk moths in local gardens.
The narra, our national tree, sheds its compound leaves during the dry season to conserve water before blooming with yellow flowers.
Filipino marine biologist Angel Alcala pioneered coral reef transplantation in Dumaguete to restore underwater biodiversity damaged by destructive fishing methods.
Ifugao farmers built stone-walled rice terraces utilizing a gravity-fed irrigation system that channels mountain rainwater through observable hollow bamboo pipes.
During the Pahiyas festival, locals decorate houses with kiping, leaf-shaped wafers made from ground rice paste dyed with natural plant extracts.
The South Sea pearl, our national gem, forms inside the Pinctada maxima oyster when an irritant triggers the observable secretion of nacre.
The carabao, our national animal, lacks functional sweat glands and cools its large body by wallowing in observable local mud and water.
Taal Volcano, which shaped local history through major eruptions, is an observable complex caldera featuring a main crater lake within Lake Taal.
The carabao mango, our national fruit, turns from green to observable yellow when its skin produces ethylene gas during the ripening process.
The anahaw, our national leaf, features large, circular fan-shaped leaves with observable veins that naturally shed water during heavy monsoon rains.
Filipino scientist Ramon Barba discovered that spraying a potassium nitrate solution on mango trees induces observable flowering even during the dry season.
